fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant of the people "…obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of the prophet Haggai…" (Haggai 1:12). They hear it, and they obey.

Waiting is a smooth move, I'll give you that. In Haggai 1:2 the people had said, "The time has not yet come…" But this time the text says they obeyed the voice of the LORD, and it doesn't say they waited for anything (Haggai 1:12).
I see why you picked it, friend. But the word in the text is "sent." The people obeyed Haggai because the LORD their God had sent him (Haggai 1:12). It's about who stood behind the prophet.
I can see why you'd pick it, baker. But the verse says they obeyed because the LORD their God had "sent" him (Haggai 1:12). The reason the text gives is who sent Haggai.

There it is. "I am with you…" declares the LORD (Haggai 1:13). Haggai delivers those four little words to the people who just obeyed. I think that's about the best thing you could hear right when you're about to roll up your sleeves.

Yes, begin! The text says "…they came and began the work on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God…" (Haggai 1:14). The LORD had called His house a ruin (Haggai 1:9), and now the work on it starts. Every big job has a first day, and this is theirs.
Finishing is the fun part, I know. But the verse says they "began" the work on the house of the LORD of Hosts (Haggai 1:14). This verse is about the start of the work, not the end.

Inspecting sounds like something a committee would do, friend, with clipboards and serious faces. But the text says they came and "began" the work (Haggai 1:14). Begin is the word in the verse, and inspect isn't in it.
Cyrus, king of Persia, is a real king in the Bible (Ezra 1:1), so it's a fair guess. But Haggai 1:15 says the work began in the second year of King Darius. Cyrus isn't named in this passage.
